key_insight: Local neural operators can act as data-driven surrogates for complex dynamical systems, allowing researchers to study stability and bifurcations without writing explicit equations or running expensive full simulations. By pairing them with equation-free and Krylov subspace methods, the paper enables system-level analysis directly from data.
problem_solved: Traditional stability and bifurcation analysis of spatiotemporal systems usually requires explicit governing equations and costly brute-force simulation. This paper addresses the challenge of extracting system-level behavior from data when the equations are unknown, incomplete, or too expensive to simulate at scale.
method: Train local neural operators to approximate the evolution of spatially extended dynamical systems from data.
Embed these learned operators into an equation-free analysis pipeline to estimate macroscopic behavior.
Use Krylov subspace techniques to efficiently compute stability-related quantities and perform bifurcation analysis.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how learned operators can move beyond prediction and become tools for scientific discovery and analysis. It expands the role of neural surrogates from fast emulation to interpretable, system-level decision support in complex physical and biological systems.

paper_title: Enabling local neural operators to perform equation-free system-level analysis
paper_authors: Gianluca Fabiani, Hannes Vandecasteele, Somdatta Goswami, Constantinos Siettos, Ioannis G. Kevrekidis
